analysis.title: EcoWeek 26.40: US Midterms: The cost of living is now a pivotal issue
key_insights: Editorial: US growth is holding up and unemployment is low, but cost of living weighs on households and Republicans could lose Congress in the 3 November midterms. Polls suggest the House could swing to the Democrats.
September CPI was 3.7% y/y versus 2.4% before the Middle East conflict began, and energy accounts for the entire gap. Gasoline rose 46% between February and October because of the Iran war.
Prices are up 28% over five years (31% for housing, 29% for food). Perceived inflation is well above measured inflation because fuel is a visible, unavoidable expense.

Wage growth is slowing as inflation re-accelerates. Average hourly earnings rose 3% y/y in September, the slowest since 2018 and below inflation, and real wages fell 0.7% y/y. Six of nine months in 2026 showed a decline.

Consumption resilience rests on a narrow base of high earners (mostly households above USD 125,000 a year) helped by stock-market wealth effects. The saving rate fell to 3.8% as households draw down savings.
The labour market is stagnant with low hiring and low firing. Payroll growth averages 68,000 a month since January versus nearly 200,000 in 2011-2019. A shrinking workforce keeps unemployment low.

Housing has deteriorated most. Mortgage rates rose from under 4% to over 7%, a lock-in effect keeps prices from falling and pushes rents up, and higher monthly repayments are not captured in inflation figures.

The next Congress will have little room to act on affordability because neither party can override the filibuster or a presidential veto. BNP sees mortgage rates staying around 7% at best given a 4.8% 10-year yield forecast for end-2027.

Fiscal and market stakes of the vote: the debt limit could be reached as early as Q1 2027, and the deficit is expected to stay at 6.3% of GDP in 2027 with upside risk if Democrats win both houses. Divided government has historically meant legislative stability.

AI sector exposure to the midterms is through sentiment and the medium term rather than legislation. A Democratic sweep could bring more congressional activism on AI regulation, concentration, data-centre electricity costs and jobs. 36 governors' seats are also up and governors control data-centre authorisations.
Monetary policy link: a Democratic Senate would require President Trump to pick a consensus nominee to replace Governor Powell from 2028 or to fill any other Fed Board vacancy.

Fed held at 3.75-4.0% with two members voting for a 25 bp hike. Chair Warsh cited stronger growth and inflation that remains too high. Q3 US GDP rose 3.4% annualised with business investment up 12.7%.

Fed, ECB and BoJ stayed on hold and are on track for December hikes. The tech sell-off in equities intensified despite strong earnings as markets balk at large capex plans, which helped bond yields ease from recent highs.

Eurozone Q3 GDP grew 0.4% q/q (0.2% ex-Ireland) and BNP raised its 2027 growth forecast to 1.6%. Bank lending conditions tightened for businesses, led by France and Germany. The ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.5% and signalled a likely final hike in December.

Lagarde confirmed she will step down early on 7 February. Official candidates named are Pablo Hernandez de Cos and Klaas Knot, and EU leaders are expected to decide the Board successions at their mid-December meeting.

France: Q3 GDP fell 0.1% q/q, Fitch moved its rating outlook to negative, HICP rose to 3.8% y/y in October and household confidence fell to 80, matching its 2013 low. BNP cut 2026 growth to 0.3% and forecasts 0.8% for 2027.
Germany: Q3 GDP rose 0.2% q/q, HICP inflation fell to 2.8% on energy-tax cuts and the Ifo index hit a three-year high. Italy: HICP jumped to 5.6% on regulated energy prices and Q3 GDP was flat.

UK: the budget was cautious and slightly expansionary, the OBR cut 2027 growth to 1%, and markets price a near-certain Bank of England hike to 4% this week. BNP agrees on the hike but does not expect further hikes. GBP hit a six-week high versus USD and a 19-month high versus EUR.

Japan: the BoJ held at 1.25% with one dissent for a hike and judged underlying inflation consistent with 2%. It will nearly triple ETF sales to about JPY 860 billion a year from January, and the next hike is expected in December.

China: the PBOC will make the overnight rate its principal policy lever from 2 November. Chinese equities fell 8.5% in October, their worst month since 2016, and the official manufacturing PMI dropped below 50 at 49.3.

Brazil: Lula's win triggered a sharp sell-off. The Ibovespa fell 14% on Monday and 18% on the week, the real fell over 11% intraday, and the 10-year yield rose 250 bp to 15.5%, driven by fiscal concerns.

Energy: European gas (TTF) breached EUR 100/MWh for the first time since December 2022 on geopolitical tension, low EU stocks and cold-snap speculation. Oil is swinging between escalation fears and hopes of renewed negotiations.

Markets overview: the Nasdaq is down about 10% from its peak after a third straight weekly tech sell-off. Europe outperformed and bonds rallied on safe-haven demand, and the bund-OAT spread is back at 164.

Calendar ahead: US midterms (Tuesday), ISM manufacturing (Monday) and non-manufacturing (Wednesday), Q3 productivity (Thursday), October payrolls (Friday), Eurozone October flash CPI (Wednesday), and the Bank of England decision (Thursday).

sector_views.rationale: Legislative risk from the midterms is low given the president's pro-AI stance and veto. The risk is sentiment and tighter regulation in the medium term after a Democratic sweep, which could weigh on valuations.

risk_factors: Iran conflict escalation keeping energy-driven inflation elevated.
US debt limit could be reached as early as Q1 2027, with polarisation complicating the budget vote.
Deficit risks tilted to the upside from war costs, debt service and possible Democratic spending trade-offs.
Democratic sweep could bring AI regulation and data-centre scrutiny, weighing on sector valuations in the medium term.
Narrow consumption base: spending relies on high earners and wealth effects, while saving rates fall.
French fiscal and growth deterioration, with a possible new Fitch review as early as February.
Brazil fiscal concerns, and Türkiye lira and reserve pressure on an MSCI status warning.
European gas prices could rise further if a cold snap hits in November.
vol_and_positioning: The tech sell-off entered a third consecutive week, taking the Nasdaq down 10% from its last peak, as markets balk at large capex plans despite strong earnings.
Chinese equities fell 8.5% in October, their worst month since 2016, on doubts over AI earnings.
geopolitical: War in Iran: pushed energy prices and US inflation higher, is unpopular with voters (72% of registered voters rank ending it a top priority per AP-NORC), and its resolution is the key factor for disinflation.
Oil fluctuates between escalation fears and hopes for a return to the negotiating table.
Brazil: Lula won a fourth presidential term, triggering a sell-off on fiscal concerns over minimum wage, Bolsa Familia and free transport pledges.
Türkiye: MSCI warned it could lose emerging-market status if transparency and market supervision measures after the Fund scandal are judged insufficient.
US administration made decisions on tariffs, immigration and Iran without Congress, and BNP expects that to continue.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth is robust at 3.4% annualised in Q3, unemployment is low and aggregate consumption is holding up, supported by wealth effects among top earners.
tension_points.bear_case: Spending rests on a narrow base of households earning over USD 125,000 a year, real wages are falling 0.7% y/y, the saving rate is down to 3.8% and the labour market is stagnant.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued decline in the saving rate or a further stock-market drop that erodes the wealth effect supporting high-earner spending.

tension_points.bull_case: Divided government has historically brought legislative stability, which markets view favourably.
tension_points.bear_case: Polarisation has increased and could complicate the budget vote and debt-ceiling debate, and a Democratic sweep could raise spending and AI regulation risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Debt limit being reached as early as Q1 2027 without agreement would undermine the stability view.
